## Summary

I created `/work/workspace.dsl` — a minimal Structurizr DSL C4 model of the parcel delivery tracking platform.

**Model elements:**
| Element | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Customer | person | Looks up parcel status |
| Parcel Tracker | softwareSystem | Owned/operated by our company |
| └ Web Portal | container | Customers look up shipments |
| └ Dispatch Service | container | Assigns parcels to couriers |
| └ Pricing Rules Library | container | Shared; computes price from weight + zone |
| └ Parcel Tracker Database | container | Stores shipments & dispatch records |
| Email Delivery Provider | softwareSystem | Operated by a different organization |

**Relationships:** Customer→Web Portal, Web Portal→Pricing Library, Dispatch Service→Pricing Library, Dispatch Service→Email Provider, Web Portal→Database, Dispatch Service→Database.

**Errors the Structurizr MCP tools reported (all fixed):**
1. `database` keyword isn't allowed nested in a `softwareSystem` → used `container` (a database is a C4 container).
2. `externalSoftwareSystem` keyword isn't supported in this DSL version → used `softwareSystem` with a description noting it's operated by a different organization.
3. Top-level `relationships` block isn't valid → moved relationship statements inside the `model` block.
4. A parent can't have a relationship to its own nested child (`parcelTracker -> database`) → attributed the database relationships to the two containers that own that data.

**One note on the `inspect` linter:** it also emits best-practice recommendations (no views, no technology on elements/relationships, no scope, no documentation/decisions). I deliberately did **not** add those, because doing so would introduce content beyond what the situation describes — directly contradicting your "keep the model minimal" instruction. The authoritative `validate` check passes with no errors, and the final file on disk is byte-for-byte the text I last validated.
